    E6 LINK INTERVENORS RESPONSE TO ONCOR ELECTRIC DELIVERY
   COMPANY LLC AND LCRA TRANSMISSION SERVICES CORPORATION'S
   OBJECTIONS TO, AND MOTION TO STRIKE, INTERVENOR TESTIMONY



TO THE       HONORABLE    CASSANDRA QUINN          DEE AND MARLO          CHICO,

ADMINISTRATIVE LAW JUDGES:

      COMES NOW, E6 Link Intervenors and files this response to Oncor and LCRA

Transmission Services Corporation's Objections to, and Motion to Strike Intervenor

Testimony.



                                        1
                                        I.   BACKGROUND

          1.       Pursuant to SOAH Order No. 6, Expert Scott R. Lucas and Intervenor

Audra Marie Walentitsch and filed their respective direct testimonies on May 13, 2026.

On May 18, 2026, Applicants filed objections to those testimonies. Applicants objected in

part to the testimony of Audra Marie Walentitsch (item no. 4467) and objected in whole

to the testimony of Scott R. Lucas (item no. 4456). Intervenors file this Response in

opposition to Applicants' objections and respectfully request that the Administrative Law

Judges overrule the objections and admit the challenged testimony.

                           II.     ARGUMENT AND AUTHORITIES

A. SCOITR. LUCAS


          2.       Applicants' objection to the testimony of Scott R. Lucas should be overruled

because the testimony is relevant to the Commission's evaluation of the impacts

associated with the proposed E6 route and provides context regarding the residential

nature of the affected area and the potential consequences of routing a 765-kV

transmission line through those properties.

          3.       Intervenors acknowledge that PURA § 37.056(c)             and   16 TAC §

25.101(b)(3)(B) do not expressly identify "property values" as an independent routing

factor.        However,   the    Commission's   rules   do   require   consideration of route

characteristics, including the use of or paralleling of existing rights-of-way, minimizing

impacts to landowners, and evaluating the comparative impacts associated with

                                                 2
 proposed routes.1 Mr. Lucas's testimony is relevant to those considerations because it

addresses the nature and extent of the residential and rural residential properties affected

by the E6 route and explains the types of impacts that high-voltage transmission line

easements can have on such properties.

        4.      Mr. Lucas does not offer testimony regarding compensation in a

condemnation proceeding, nor does he provide a formal appraisal of any specific

property along the proposed route. In fact, his testimony expressly states that he has "not

performed an appraisal of any property along the proposed E6 route" and is "not offering

opinions of value on any specific property or group of properties." Instead, he provides

general market-based testimony derived from his professional experience and prior case

studies involving high-voltage transmission line easements and their impacts on

property marketability and diminution.

        5.      His testimony is also relevant because Applicants themselves placed

comparative route costs and route impacts at issue in this proceeding. Mr. Lucas's

testimony provides context regarding the characteristics of the E6 route, including the

number of residential properties and habitable structures affected, and explains why




1 Applicants themselves recognize that while property values are not an express standalone routing factor
under PURA § 37.056(c) or 16 TAC § 25.101(b)(3)(B), the Commission nevertheless considers routing
impacts associated with existing rights-of-way and impacts to affected landowners. 5ee Direct Testimony
of Lawrence Rahmes, P.IE., Infrastructure Division, Public Utility Commission of Texas at 28, PUC Docket
No. 59336, Item No. 2014 (Apr. 24, 2026).


                                                   3
 routing transmission infrastructure through residential areas may create significant

impacts to affected landowners.

       6.      To the extent Applicants disagree with Mr. Lucas's opinions, methodology,

or conclusions, those arguments go to the weight of the evidence rather than

admissibility. Mr. Lucas is a licensed appraiser with substantial experience evaluating

the impacts of transmission line easements on real property. Any disagreement regarding

the significance or persuasiveness of his testimony is properly addressed through cross-

examination and competing evidence, not exclusion. Accordingly, Applicants' objection

should be overruled.


B. AUDRA MARIE WALENTITSCH

       7.      Applicants' objection to Mrs. Walentitsch's testimony and supporting

exhibit should likewise be overruled. Mrs. Walentitsch's testimony regarding the impact

the proposed transmission line has had on her property value is relevant to the issues

before the Commission and is permissible lay testimony from a property owner

regarding her own property.

       8.      Texas law has long recognized that property owners are competent to

testify regarding the value of their own property . Reid Rd . Mun . Util . Dist . No . 2 v . Speedy

Stop Food Stores, Ltd., 337 S.W.3d 846, 853 (Tex. 2011). Mrs. Walentitsch's testimony

concerning the reduction in her property value constitutes a lay opinion based on her

ownership, familiarity with the property, and personal knowledge of the effects the

                                                4
 proposed route has had on the property's marketability and perceived value. Her

testimony is therefore admissible as lay opinion testimony and does not improperly

constitute undisclosed expert testimony.

       9.     Further, the Bell County Appraisal District notice attached to her testimony

is an official record of a governmental entity. Intervenors are not offering the document

as a formal expert appraisal establishing a definitive valuation figure. Rather, the exhibit

is offered to show what Mrs. Walentitsch received from the Bell County Appraisal District

and to provide context and support for her concerns regarding the effect the proposed

transmission line may have on her property value.

       10.    The testimony and exhibit are also relevant because they demonstrate the

concerns held by affected property owners regarding the potential impacts of the

proposed E6 route. Applicants have placed route impacts at issue in this proceeding, and

testimony regarding perceived and actual impacts to residential property values is

relevant to the Commission's evaluation of the route.

       11.    To the extent Applicants disagree with the conclusions Mrs. Walentitsch

draws from the appraisal district notice or dispute the amount of any alleged diminution

in value, those arguments go to the weight and credibility of the evidence rather than its

admissibility. Applicants remain free to cross-examine Mrs. Walentitsch regarding her

opinions and the attached records, but exclusion of the testimony and exhibit is not

warranted.



                                             5
                         III.   CONCLUSION AND PRAYER

       12.   WHEREFORE, PREMISES CONSIDERED, Intervenors respectfully

request that the Administrative Law Judges overrule Applicants' objections to the

testimony and exhibits of Scott R. Lucas and Audra Marie Walentitsch in their entirety

and admit the challenged testimony and exhibits into the record. The challenged

testimony is relevant to the Commission's consideration of the proposed E6 route and

any alleged deficiencies raised by Applicants go to the weight of the evidence, not its

admissibility. Intervenors further request all other relief to which they may be justly

entitled.
